label: Applied Baconian scientific empiricism to the systemic study of human society
description: Auguste Comte adopted Francis Bacon's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Francis Bacon's perspective to Auguste Comte's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Early Modern & Scientific across history into the 19th Century Divergences.

label: Formulated the theological, metaphysical, and positive stages of civilizational development
description: Auguste Comte formulated and introduced the concept of "Law of the Three Stages", which became a seminal contribution in social-theory philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in social-theory.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 19th Century Divergences as part of Auguste Comte's canonical writings.

label: Mill engaged with and critiqued Comte's positivism in formulating his own sociological logic
description: John Stuart Mill was fundamentally influenced by Auguste Comte's central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Auguste Comte's perspective to John Stuart Mill's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the 19th Century Divergences era.

label: Durkheim transformed Comtean positivist sociology into institutional academic research
description: Émile Durkheim adopted Auguste Comte's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Auguste Comte's perspective to Émile Durkheim's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the 19th Century Divergences era.
